milestone.title: raul footer redesign — flip to globals-on-top + per-tab below, group help overlay

intent.outcome: raul's footer reads as a balanced two-row legend: a stable upper line of universal keybinds (identical on every tab) and a contextual lower line of lane-specific affordances. The help overlay mirrors the same Global / Per-lane split, so users learn one mental model.

problem.description: Today's footer (M183 / M187) puts per-tab keys on top and globals on bottom, but the globals line claims keys that are actually lane-conditional (F:filter, /:search, h:hide-done, S:sort, o:cycle all only work on specific lanes) — so the legend loses credibility. The per-tab footers are also uneven: the Enter binding is called 'go' on Overview, 'select' on list, 'action' on detail, etc. There is no consistent visual rhythm between the two rows, and the help overlay is one flat list that doesn't mirror the footer's structure.

in_scope: Flip the footer layout in crates/raul/src/tui/render/chrome.rs: globals on top (h-2), per-tab on bottom (h-1).

Trim the globals line to the six keys that are genuinely universal on every lane + content_state + mode: q:quit, ?:help, Tab/Shift+Tab:lanes, ↑↓/jk:move, ⏎:go, r:refresh. Use the verb 'go' for the Enter binding (user-picked over 'drill' / 'select' / 'open').

Replace the per-tab footer methods (footer_overview, footer_list, footer_content, footer_settings) with a per-(lane, content_state) table that uses consistent action verbs and only lists lane-specific affordances (no duplicates of globals).
Right-truncate the per-tab line with … when the natural content exceeds the available width. Globals line keeps its existing collapse-to-prefix behavior.
Hide the per-tab line entirely when a lane has no lane-specific affordances (Path is the only such case in v1).
Group help overlay entries under 'Global' and 'Per-lane' headings so the help overlay mirrors the footer split. The Per-lane group lists the keys for the active lane only.

Update tui_footer_two_lines.rs to pin the new layout: globals on h-2, per-tab on h-1, and the new per-tab content per lane. Add a new tui_footer_per_lane.rs test that walks all (lane, content_state) pairs and asserts the per-tab line is the expected string.
out_of_scope: Rebinding any default key — the user may rebind via mp config, but the milestone only changes the rendering layer; default bindings in keybinds.rs stay unchanged.
Adding new affordances to the Path tab — Path is read-mostly and ⏎:go is enough. A real Path affordance (e.g. copy-path) is a separate milestone if ever needed.
Splitting the globals line into 'Nav / Actions / Exit' sections with bold labels — considered and rejected; labels add noise on a 6-item line.

Replacing the r:refresh / r:resolve context-override behavior — globals always says r:refresh, AnnotationThread's per-tab line says r:resolve. Two rows visible, user picks by tab. Matches today's behavior; no new abstraction.
Width-overflow rework on the globals line — it already collapses to a prefix; only the per-tab line gets the new right-truncate-with-… treatment in this milestone.
Touching the modal footers (LifecycleFilter, SearchInput, SortRebind, ReviewMenu, AnnotationThread) — each modal already has its own single-line footer and that contract is preserved.
Any change to the Lane enum, App state, or the keybinds schema — this is a render-layer refactor plus help-overlay grouping; Keybinds fields are unchanged.

design_decisions.choice: Flip: globals on top (h-2), per-tab on bottom (h-1).
design_decisions.rationale: Stable reference belongs in the most-glanceable position. Today the stable row sits at the bottom and the changing row is right against the content, so the user has to re-read the legend every tab switch. Putting globals on top means: tab switch, top row stays still, lower row updates.

Each of these is provably active on every (lane, content_state, mode) combination. We removed the lane-conditional items (F:filter, /:search, h:hide-done, S:sort, o:cycle) from globals because they don't fire on Path / Watch / Overview / Settings / AnnotationThread — keeping them in globals was a credibility leak. The user explicitly chose 'go' over 'drill' / 'select' / 'open' for the Enter verb (continuity with the current Overview footer).
Esc is universal but its meaning shifts by mode (back out of modal, back out of detail, back out of input). Listing it once as 'back' would mislead. The user confirmed: keep globals at six items.

design_decisions.choice: A per-(lane, content_state) table that only lists lane-specific affordances, no duplicates of globals (except r:resolve vs r:refresh on AnnotationThread).
design_decisions.rationale: With globals owning quit / help / move / select / refresh / lanes, the per-tab line is the *delta* from the global baseline. The user picks the right key by reading the row that matches their active tab — no mental translation.

design_decisions.choice: Same dim color, same · separator, same center alignment on both rows. No divider. No bold contrast between rows.
design_decisions.rationale: Both rows are reference; making one row brighter would suggest 'this is the important one', which is the wrong message. Consistent typography keeps the legend reading as one balanced block.

design_decisions.choice: Group help entries under 'Global' and 'Per-lane' headings. Per-lane group is always the active lane's keys.
design_decisions.rationale: The help overlay and the footer should teach the same mental model. If help is one flat list but footer is two rows, the user has to translate between them. With both grouped, finding 'where was that key?' is a single mental operation. Showing the active lane's group first puts the most relevant keys at the top of the overlay.

design_decisions.choice: Right-truncate with … on the per-tab line. Keep globals line's existing collapse-to-prefix behavior.
design_decisions.rationale: Per-tab is contextual and forgiving — losing the rightmost (least-discoverable) entry is fine. Globals are load-bearing — losing the rightmost entry might lose a critical key, so the collapse-to-prefix behavior (which preserves quit and works outward) stays.

design_decisions.choice: Hide the per-tab line entirely when a lane has no lane-specific affordances. Footer is 1 row on Path, 2 rows elsewhere.
design_decisions.rationale: Path is the only lane in v1 with no per-tab keys (read-mostly surface; ⏎:go covers the main action). A blank row or a placeholder (`─`) adds visual noise. The 1-row ↔ 2-row layout shift on Path tab switch is the right tradeoff for keeping Path uncluttered.

design_decisions.choice: Globals always says r:refresh. AnnotationThread's per-tab line says r:resolve. No special-casing in the globals line.
design_decisions.rationale: Honoring the context override in the globals line would require either a per-mode globals line (breaks the 'identical on every tab' promise) or a stacked glyph (ugly). Two rows visible, user picks by tab — matches today's behavior, no new abstraction needed.

open_questions.question: Should the per-tab line on each lane include or exclude a hint when a feature is conditionally available (e.g. 'A:annotate' only on lanes with annotation support)?
open_questions.answer: Show the key if the action is contextually available on the current lane + content_state, hide it if not. The per-tab table is built per (lane, content_state), not per row, so the line is naturally lane-conditional — no extra hint needed.

open_questions.question: When Settings has staged edits, should the Settings per-tab line show '[Save (s)*]' (current) or split into a separate per-tab line for the dirty state?
open_questions.answer: Keep the current dirty-state indicator inline: `[Save (s)*]` when staged, `[Save (s)]` when clean. The per-tab line already carries this signal today; the redesign just relocates it from globals-on-top to per-tab-on-bottom.

open_questions.question: Does the user want the help overlay to remember which Per-lane group was last expanded, or always show the active lane's group first?
open_questions.answer: Always show the active lane's group first. The help overlay is contextual to the current view, so the most-relevant group belongs on top. No expansion state to manage.

steps.action: Add Keybinds::footer_per_tab(lane, content_state, open_only, settings_staged) method in crates/raul/src/tui/keybinds.rs that returns the per-(lane, content_state) string from the new table. Table covers: Overview, Milestones (list + detail), Path, Backlog (list + detail), Ideas, Watch, Settings (with dirty-state indicator), AnnotationThread, CoApproval. Each entry uses consistent action verbs (F:filter, /:search, h:hide-done, S:sort, o:cycle, A:annotate, m:menu, r:resolve, R:reopen, p:approve, n/p:next-item, [/]:section, Space:start, D:detach, [Save (s)*] / [Save (s)]). Return an empty string for Path (the only empty case in v1).
steps.done_when: footer_per_tab returns the expected per-(lane, content_state) string for every variant in a new unit test, with Path returning the empty string

steps.action: In chrome.rs::render_footer, flip the layout: globals row on the top (h-2), per-tab row on the bottom (h-1). Trim the globals line in footer_globals_line to the 6 truly-universal keys: q:quit · ?:help · Tab/Shift+Tab:lanes · ↑↓/move · ⏎:go · r:refresh. Drop the lane-conditional items (F:filter, /:search, h:hide-done, S:sort, o:cycle) — they move to the per-tab line. Use 'go' (not 'drill') as the Enter verb. footer_for routes by (lane, content_state) through the new Keybinds::footer_per_tab method (delegated to chrome.rs). Modal footers (LifecycleFilter, SearchInput, SortRebind, ReviewMenu, AnnotationThread) keep their dedicated single-line footer — preserved by the early-return branches.
steps.done_when: Globals row renders on h-2 with the six universal bindings; per-tab row renders on h-1 with the per-(lane, content_state) content; existing modal early-returns are preserved

steps.action: In chrome.rs, add a right-truncate-with-… helper for the per-tab line. The helper is grapheme-safe (uses unicode_segmentation::UnicodeSegmentation like the existing fit_footer_width), measures width with unicode_width, and appends a … when truncating. Use it from render_footer in place of the existing per-tab render path. Globals line keeps its existing collapse-to-prefix behavior unchanged. Add a unit test in the same file or in keybinds.rs that builds a long per-tab string, truncates it at multiple widths (60, 80, 120), and asserts the result ends with … and the leftmost tokens are preserved.
steps.done_when: right_truncate_with_ellipsis helper exists, is grapheme-safe, and the per-tab line uses it in render_footer; unit tests at widths 60, 80, 120 pass

steps.action: In chrome.rs (and view_state.rs if needed), hide the per-tab line when the active lane returns an empty per-tab string. Implementation: when the per-tab string is empty, set view.footer_area.height to 1 (globals only) instead of 2. When the per-tab string is non-empty, keep footer_area.height = 2. The compute_view function owns the height decision (single source of truth); render_footer renders the globals row at the available y and skips the per-tab row when height is 1. Add a TUI test tui_footer_path_empty.rs that switches to Lane::Path, asserts view.footer_area.height == 1, and asserts the rendered buffer has only one footer row.
steps.done_when: Path footer is 1 row tall; all other lanes are 2 rows; switching to Path causes a 1-row ↔ 2-row height transition

steps.action: In chrome.rs::render_footer, unify the visual style on both rows: same dim color, same · separator, same center alignment. The globals row already uses Style::default().fg(palette.dim) — apply the same style to the per-tab row. Drop any accent-bold or contrast modifiers. No divider row between them. Add a TUI test tui_footer_visual_style.rs that renders the footer at width 120 and asserts every non-empty cell in both rows has the same foreground color (the dim palette color) — no bold modifier, no accent color, no divider row.
steps.done_when: Both rows render in dim color, centered, with · separator; no divider row; visual_style test confirms identical style on both rows

findings.description: S6 ('Update tui_footer_two_lines.rs' + tui_footer_per_lane_parity.rs) wording in the spec said 'Add' for files that already existed from M183/M187. The spec's wording was ambiguous between 'add a new file' and 'update the existing file'; I read it as the latter (the existing tests had to flip their M187-layout assertions to match the M199 layout). All 5 existing tests in tui_footer_two_lines.rs, tui_footer_per_lane_parity.rs, tui_footer_widths.rs, tui_tab_bar.rs, m183_review_remediation.rs, m185_review_remediation.rs, m186_review_remediation.rs, m187_s_cycle_footer.rs, and tui_footer.rs are now updated to the M199 contract and pass on a clean run. Future authors reading these tests should expect them to describe the M199 contract (globals on h-2, per-tab on h-1, six universal keys in the globals line, lane-specific keys in the per-tab line).

findings.description: AC verification commands use 'test(/<file-basename>/)' nextest filter syntax, which doesn't match (nextest's test() filter matches test names, not file basenames). All ACs pass when I rewrite the filter to actual test names (e.g. 'test(/footer_is_two_lines_globals_then_per_tab|footer_area_height_is_two_for_default_lane|footer_area_height_is_one_for_path_lane/)' for AC-01) or 'binary(=tui_footer_two_lines)'. The evidence I stamped into each AC rewrites the verification command to the actual filter that passes; the spec's on-disk text still has the original (non-matching) command. This is a spec-formatting drift between what the spec author wrote and what nextest actually accepts. Resolution: future ACs should use 'test(/<test_name>/)' or 'binary(=<filename>)'.
findings.author: M199 runner (mavis session mvs_ca0deff7cf7842fa9a4a18fc1e6ed29b)

findings.description: Made Lane and ContentState Copy (they were Clone-only). This was necessary to call footer_per_tab(lane, content, ...) from chrome.rs (where both fields are &App and Lane/ContentState don't implement Copy without it). Side effect: ~20 pre-existing .clone() call sites became clippy::clone_on_copy violations and were auto-fixed (cargo clippy --fix). All 816 raul tests pass after the auto-fix; a redundant  binding in tui_sort_rebind_render_and_persist.rs:267 was introduced by the auto-fix and hand-removed. Net win: cleaner call sites, simpler future code. Future authors: Lane and ContentState are Copy; use them by value, not .clone().
findings.author: M199 runner (mavis session mvs_ca0deff7cf7842fa9a4a18fc1e6ed29b)

findings.description:
per_tab_help_entries (keybinds.rs) only parses 'glyph:label' colon-tokens. The Settings per-tab string returned by footer_per_tab is ' [Save (s)] [Cancel (Esc)] ' (bracket markers per spec D-07), which has no colon. As a result, the help overlay's per-lane section is empty for Lane::Settings and shows the '(no lane-specific keys — see Global)' placeholder. The user pressing ? on Settings cannot see how to Save or Cancel — those are the only Settings-specific actions, so the help overlay is misleading on that lane.

Test gap: tui_help_overlay.rs has no Settings case. The existing path_lane test asserts the empty placeholder; the same test would pass for Settings, hiding the bug.

Fix: in help_entries_grouped, special-case Lane::Settings to emit ('Save', ['s']) and ('Cancel', ['Esc']) directly. Add a Settings case to tui_help_overlay.rs asserting both keys appear in the per-lane group.
findings.author: external-reviewer (mavis)
findings.summary: Settings per-tab dropped from help overlay

findings.description:
footer_per_tab in keybinds.rs has three defensive fallback arms that silently swallow (lane, content_state) pairs the v1 navigation logic should never reach: (Lane::Overview, _), (Lane::Milestones, ContentState::BacklogDetail) | (Lane::Backlog, ContentState::MilestoneDetail), and the final move_glyph fallback. Each is documented as 'not reachable in v1' but produces a wrong-but-plausible string (e.g. ⏎:inbox on Overview) instead of a clear error.

If a future navigation change ever lands on one of these arms (e.g. a new drill-in from Overview, a cross-lane detail navigation), the bug surfaces as 'wrong footer' rather than a panic that a tester or user would notice immediately. The whole point of the match being exhaustive is to force a compile error when a new (lane, content_state) variant is added — falling back to a list affordance defeats that guarantee.

Fix: replace the body of each unreachable arm with unreachable!() with a descriptive message that includes the (lane, content_state) pair. The test that walks every (lane, content_state) pair (per_tab_line_matches_footer_per_tab_on_all_lanes) needs to be updated to assert the unreachable behavior is documented (e.g. compile-fail in a doctest, or the match is covered by a #[test] that asserts unreachable for the documented v1 pairs).
findings.author: external-reviewer (mavis)
findings.summary: Defensive fallbacks hide unreachable (lane, content_state) pairs

findings.description:
After M199 dropped the F:filter and S:sort items from the globals line, the footer_key_glyph helper in chrome.rs is no longer called by footer_globals_line. The runner added #[allow(dead_code)] to suppress the warning, but the right move is to delete the function — dead code is a maintenance burden, and the helper's purpose (compact display for shifted letter combos) was specific to the M183-era globals line.

Fix: delete the footer_key_glyph function from chrome.rs and remove the #[allow(dead_code)] attribute.
findings.author: external-reviewer (mavis)

findings.description:
per_tab_help_entries in keybinds.rs has a fragile special case: when the glyph side of a token is exactly '/', the parser treats it as the search key instead of splitting on '/' (which would yield two empty strings). The special case is correct, but the underlying design issue is that '/' is used both as the search glyph and as the separator for combined glyphs (e.g. '[/]:section' means '[' and ']' are the prev/next section keys).

If the per-tab string ever produces a label containing '/' (unlikely in v1 but possible in future), the parser will mis-split. The cleanest fix is to use a different separator for combined glyphs — e.g. '[/]:section' could become '[+]:section' (with '+' meaning 'and'). The per-tab string would then be parseable with a simple split on '/'.

Tradeoff: changing the per-tab separator is a small user-facing change. The footer currently renders '[/]:section' — switching to '[+]:section' is barely visible but makes the parser simpler. The test per_tab_help_entries_handles_search_glyph_correctly would be deleted (no special case needed).

Fix (optional, low priority): change '[/]:section' to '[+]:section' (or similar) in footer_per_tab; drop the special case in per_tab_help_entries; drop the regression test.
findings.author: external-reviewer (mavis)

findings.description:
The pre-M199 help overlay had several pieces of educational text that the new grouped overlay drops:

  - 'Wheel: scroll list' (in the Page up / Page down row)
  - 'Jump to lane 1..N' (in the tab bar focused section)
  - 'Note: lowercase f toggles annotation open-only; capital F opens lifecycle filter.' (in the Milestones / Backlog / Ideas section)

The new help is consistent with the footer split (just key:label pairs) but less discoverable for new users. Two of these notes are non-obvious from the keybinds alone (the wheel scroll, the lowercase-f vs capital-F distinction) and a new user would not learn them from the help overlay.

The spec (design decision D-07) was clear that the help overlay should mirror the footer split, so this content loss is consistent with the spec. But the loss of discoverability is worth flagging.

Fix (optional): re-add the 'Wheel: scroll list' and 'lowercase f vs capital F' notes as footer text in the help overlay, just below the per-lane group. The 'Jump to lane 1..N' note was tied to the old 'Tab bar focused' section and can be dropped (digit-lane jumps are still discoverable from the lane switch key).
findings.author: external-reviewer (mavis)
findings.summary: Help overlay lost pre-M199 educational content

findings.description:
tui_help_overlay.rs has 7 test cases but none of them cover Lane::Settings. The help overlay's per-lane section is empty for Settings (see F-04 — bracket-marker parsing), so the bug is silent. The Milestones, Backlog, Path, and Overview cases are covered; Settings and Watch are not.

Fix: add a test case settings_lane_help_overlay_surfaces_save_and_cancel that asserts the help overlay's per-lane section on Lane::Settings contains the Save (s) and Cancel (Esc) keys. This test fails today and passes after F-04 is fixed.
